requirement:
Each assessment MUST have a separate JSON usage record under
`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using
{cite}`requirements.configuration.state_location`.
It MUST identify its format version, run, project root, subject kind and full
name, start time, backend and model when known, end time when finished, outcome,
accepted determination kind (`true`, `false`, or `FIXME`) when present, and
whether evidence was written. It MUST record the selected output destination in
`evidence_output` as `file` or `stdout`; a successful write to either destination
MUST set `evidence_written` to true. Usage recording MUST remain outside the
project in stdout mode. FIXME entry text MUST NOT be stored in usage records.
Failed, cancelled, or unfinished
runs MUST remain distinguishable from completed judgments. Records MUST persist
for later review without storing source text, prompts, responses, or rationale.
rationale:
**Verdict.** The implementation covers every obligation in `requirements.authoring.usage_storage`, the markings are complete, and the tests cover the main points and failure cases. One small marking oddity is noted below and does not change the verdict.

**Implementation**
- **Location and file name.** `UsageLog::start` (`src/authoring/usage.rs`) writes `<state>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json`. The run id combines nanosecond time, pid and an atomic sequence, and the file is opened with `create_new`. Each assessment gets its own file, and the confirmation follow-up conversations (`followup_log`) get their own as well.
- **State root.** `usage_state_root`, `resolved_location` and `config::state_root` take the state root from the state-location requirement.
  - Directories are created.
  - A state location inside the project is refused before anything is created, symlinks resolved. This applies in both file and stdout modes.
  - Failure to determine or create the state location is reported before any model request, and no history is claimed.
- **Required fields.** `UsageRecord` serializes the following:
  - `version` (1), `run_id`, `project_root`, `subject` (the full name or citation label), `subject_kind` (from `AssessmentKind::noun`);
  - `backend` and `model`, set when known in `configured_record`;
  - `start_time_ms` and `end_time_ms` (set only by `finish`);
  - `outcome` (`unfinished` at start, then `completed`, `failed` or `cancelled`);
  - `determination` (only the kind from `Judgment::kind`: `true`, `false` or `FIXME`; the FIXME entries are never stored);
  - `evidence_output` (`file` or `stdout`, set in `author_evidence_with_options`) and `evidence_written`.
- **Evidence written.** `evidence_written` is set to true only after a successful write to the file or to stdout (`configured_assessment`, `PendingAssessment::persisted`). It stays false if the write fails.
- **Distinguishable outcomes.** Interruption maps to `cancelled`, other errors to `failed`, and a record never finished stays `unfinished` with no end time. This holds on the single-run, batch (`prepare_assessment`, `failed`) and follow-up (`finish_followup`) paths.
- **No content stored.** The record holds counts, hashes-free metadata and fixed tool names only. Unknown tool names become `unknown`. Source text, prompts, responses and rationale are never serialized.
- **Marking.** `{impl}` markers sit on all the relevant code. `UsageLog` itself carries only a `{cite}`. It is a plain data holder, with the behaviour in the marked methods, so I treat that as immaterial.

**Tests**
- **Unit tests in `usage.rs`.**
  - The initial `unfinished` record has no end time.
  - A cancelled request persists elapsed time and incomplete token totals.
  - Source and requirement text, file names and selectors, and unknown model-supplied tool names are absent from the serialized record.
  - Determination `FIXME` and `evidence_written` are persisted.
- **`tests/authoring_cli.rs`.**
  - `usage_record_identifies_its_run_and_unusable_state_is_reported` checks the file name equals `run_id`, the version, project root, subject, kind, backend, model, `evidence_output` and start/end times. It also checks the unusable-state cases: an `XDG_STATE_HOME` that is a file, and no state location at all. Both fail with a diagnostic and write no evidence.
  - `usage_state_inside_the_project_is_refused_before_creating_it` runs in file and stdout modes and checks that no directory is created inside the project.
  - `stdout_emits_only_evidence_json_without_changing_project_files` covers stdout with `true`, `false` and FIXME. It checks `evidence_output` is `stdout` and `evidence_written` is true.
  - The main CLI test checks that the FIXME text `#125`, the rationale, and the requirement and source text are absent from usage.
  - `missing_duplicate_and_invalid_submissions_preserve_existing_evidence` covers failed runs in both output modes (`failed`, `evidence_written` false, determination null).
  - `failed_evidence_write_keeps_the_accepted_judgment_in_usage` covers the write-failure case: determination `FIXME` and `evidence_written` false.
  - The read-denial test checks failed usage.
- **`tests/authoring_batch.rs`.**
  - Usage records are counted per assessment.
  - Failed runs are distinguished from completed ones.
  - An interrupted run is `cancelled` with `evidence_written` false.

**Boundary not directly tested.** No test sends SIGINT to a single non-batch run. The shared cancellation logic is covered by the batch interruption test and the unit test.

`<state-root>/authoring/usage/<run-id>.json` using

:::{req} state_location
Habeas MUST store persistent per-user activity state under
`$XDG_STATE_HOME/habeas` on Unix when XDG_STATE_HOME is an absolute, nonempty path,
otherwise under `$HOME/.local/state/habeas`. On Windows it MUST use
`%LOCALAPPDATA%/habeas/state`. `HOME` and `LOCALAPPDATA` MUST likewise be
absolute, nonempty paths to be used. Features MUST use a named subdirectory under that
state root and document their record formats and locations.
State MUST persist across invocations and MUST NOT be stored in the project
repository, the configuration file, or a disposable cache directory. Habeas MUST
create the required directories when recording state. If it cannot determine or
write the state location, the operation requiring that state MUST report the
failure and MUST NOT claim that its history was recorded.
